But that would be in its own way untrue to Homer, who is talking about the Bronze Age but puts all kinds of Iron Age anachronisms into the story. 

We don’t know exactly why the oral tradition evolved that way, but it’s how these things tend to go.

There’s no obligation to make an inclusive Odyssey — it would be really interesting to watch an exercise along the lines of The Northman where you try as hard as possible to genuinely recreate the Bronze Age eastern Mediterranean.

You also get the converse. 

Star Trek casts tend to track the ethnic diversity of the United States of America rather than of the planet earth — they are too white in other words given actual world demographics — because these are American stories.

If we want to have a canon — which we should — it is going to be a canon of mostly old European stories, so you need to let a wide range of people into the cannon. That’s what it means to have a common culture. That’s the point.

By the same token, Denzel Washington plays Macbeth because the American dramatic tradition lays claim to the legacy of Shakespeare so great American actors challenge themselves to play these roles. It’s not a documentary about Scotland.

piped.video/HM3hsVrBMA4?si=c2nl…

This is why the authors of the Federalist papers have Latin pseudonyms, it’s why there are lots of legislatures called Senate, it’s why Trump is correct to promote classical architecture for government buildings, but it’s also why you can have a multi-racial cast of The Odyssey.
Part of the genius of “the west” as a concept is that it has always allowed people who are not in any way descended from ancient Greece or Rome to see themselves as heirs to the classical legacy.
I feel like it was easier to write influential big ideas books in the midcentury era because the norms of the period did not expect authors to assemble any kind of evidence for their claims.
